#73467. ‘More than just a game’: How GTA VI’s blockbuster launch fuels a booming content economy

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (698 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

‘More than just a game’: How GTA VI’s blockbuster launch fuels a booming content economy

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (698 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto VI has exploded out of the gate after a 13-year wait, drawing millions of buyers while fueling a parallel economy of livestreams, clips and other content built around people watching the game as much as playing it.
  • GTA VI has delivered a blockbuster debut, with about 19.1 million copies sold — including preorders — by Thursday morning, representing roughly $1.84 billion in sales, according to Sensor Tower.
  • Take-Two Interactive, which owns the studio behind the game, has not yet disclosed a profit figure for the title.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI has exploded out of the gate after a 13-year wait, drawing millions of buyers while fueling a parallel economy of livestreams, clips and other content built around people watching the game as much as playing it.

GTA VI has delivered a blockbuster debut, with about 19.1 million copies sold — including preorders — by Thursday morning, representing roughly $1.84 billion in sales, according to Sensor Tower. The GTA franchise itself has sold more than 470 million units worldwide.

Take-Two Interactive, which owns the studio behind the game, has not yet disclosed a profit figure for the title.

Ross Gerber, president and CEO of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" that he sees further upside for Take-Two, which his firm holds in its portfolio.

Sources indicate that "It's crazy good. I've never seen anything like it," Gerber noted, hailing the title as "more than just a game" and pointing to the franchise's potential to expand into film and television.

But that launch is also spawning a second economy around the enormous global hype and demand for GTA VI content.

Viewers watched 125.5 million hours of the title's content in its first 24 hours across platforms including Twitch, YouTube and Kick, according to Streams Charts.

According to recent reports, youTube creator Darren "IShowSpeed" Watkins Jr. led streamers with 4.47 million hours viewed across YouTube and Twitch. Separately, Twitch tracker CastAccord recorded about two million hours watched over roughly 36 hours of streamer Kai Cenat's launch broadcast.

Industry observers note that both creators had built anticipation with trailers for their own GTA VI coverage. As of Nov. 19, IShowSpeed's trailer had drawn 3.7 million YouTube views, while Cenat's had amassed 2.7 million.

According to Forbes, IShowSpeed and Cenat are estimated to earn about $30 million and $8.5 million a year, respectively, from their broader creator businesses.

Rockstar Games, the studio behind the franchise, has also moved to capitalize on the surge in viewer interest, partnering with YouTube on a 24-hour launch broadcast and introducing themed gifts that viewers could send during select streams.

Outside creators and agencies are also trying to capture the surge in demand for Grand Theft Auto content.

Agency Clipped & Shipped is offering a $10,000 prize pool to editors who can drive audiences to clips from Kai Cenat's streams, with qualifying submissions distributed across YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Instagram and X.

A separate campaign offered $1 per 1,000 views for clips of streamer KreekCraft, with individual submissions eligible to earn up to $400.

Those audiences could translate into thousands of dollars in creator revenue.

Recent findings suggest that using AIR Media-Tech's U.S. YouTube Shorts benchmark, 1.5 million eligible engaged views could generate about $490, while 5.1 million would yield roughly $1,670.

In a recent development, the two Vice City Dispatch videos could generate about $3,840 based on higher benchmark rates for long-form content. The channels' actual earnings could not be independently verified.

Moreover, the content economy is becoming increasingly automated.

On X, users are pitching artificial intelligence-assisted clipping operations that scan livestreams for spikes in chat activity, automatically cut highlights and distribute them across multiple accounts.

One user claimed an operation generated $21,000 overnight from 2.7 million views, equivalent to about $7.78 per 1,000 reported views.

The earnings claims could not be independently verified. X bases payouts on qualified impressions from Premium users, which are not reflected in public view counts.

And appetite for more content — and more revenue — may only be starting.

Wedbush analyst Alicia Reese told CNBC that in-game purchases could generate "years of high-margin recurring revenue" for Take-Two, which she believes investors have yet to fully price in.

She expects the console launch to be followed by a PC release and then an online multiplayer mode, mirroring the rollout of the previous title in the franchise.

According to recent reports, rockstar's launch announcement listed PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, with no timetable for either potential follow-on. GTA VI has also picked up eight nominations for the Game Awards, including game of the year, best game direction, narrative, art direction, score and music, audio design, action/adventure and performance.

Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (517 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
  • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
  • Recent findings suggest that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting big moves.

With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

Recent findings suggest that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the company that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

"Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, noted in a text ahead of the company's after-market report on Tuesday.

Industry observers note that since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is presently 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

One catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

Sources indicate that with bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

Tata Steel to buy $1.67 billion stake in India’s largest steel pipe maker; shares plunge nearly 5%

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (302 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tata Steel, one of the world's leading steel producers, on Monday stated it will buy a 26.4% stake in India's largest structural steel pipe and tube maker, APL Apollo, for 155.1 billion rupees ($1.67 billion).
  • The acquisition will boost Tata Steel's downstream integration to around 53% from 35%, the company said in a stock exchange filing.
  • Shares of Tata Steel were nearly 5% lower on Monday, while APL Apollo shares tanked over 10% in early trade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tata Steel, one of the world's leading steel producers, on Monday stated it will buy a 26.4% stake in India's largest structural steel pipe and tube maker, APL Apollo, for 155.1 billion rupees ($1.67 billion).

The acquisition will boost Tata Steel's downstream integration to around 53% from 35%, the company said in a stock exchange filing. That will lead to more value addition, improved product mix, and greater exposure to higher-margin downstream segments, it said.

Shares of Tata Steel were nearly 5% lower on Monday, while APL Apollo shares tanked over 10% in early trade.

APL Apollo stated after the deal it plans to more than double the downstream capacity to 15.5 million tons from the current 7.5 million tons, making it a leading global downstream steel firm.

This capacity addition will be completed by 2035 and would include around 9 million tons per annum of steel tubes and around 6.5 million tons per annum of color-coated products, as per Tata Steel.

Tata Steel will acquire a stake from existing shareholders of APL Apollo for 2,100 rupees per share and will ​also make an open offer to acquire an additional 26% ‌stake for 2,301.40 rupees a piece.

If the open offer is successful, Tata Steel would get a controlling stake of 52.38% in APL Apollo. World's second-largest steel maker ArcelorMittal was also reportedly in the fray to acquire APL Apollo.

The acquisition of APL Apollo would "create a downstream powerhouse for the future" that will serve the growing Indian market, T V Narendran, chief executive and managing director of Tata Steel, said in the release.

Tata Steel, which has an annual crude steel capacity of over 35 million tons per annum, is one of the world's most geographically diversified steel producers with presence across India, Europe and Thailand.

    Anthropic’s record IPO collides with tech’s worst week on Wall Street since 2020

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1272 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, startup investor Ben Narasin is so jazzed about Anthropic's blockbuster IPO that he's planning a party later this month at his Silicon Valley home.
    • "This is a celebration of the most material, significant, and mind-blowingly awesome event that has ever happened in venture capital," Narasin, founding partner of Tenacity Venture Capital, told CNBC in an interview, adding that he didn't even invest in the company.
    • Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO and an additional $26 billion from tech giants that bought at the offer price.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, startup investor Ben Narasin is so jazzed about Anthropic's blockbuster IPO that he's planning a party later this month at his Silicon Valley home. Sake, vodka and Krug Champagne will be served. Each attendee will be given two jars of caviar.

    "This is a celebration of the most material, significant, and mind-blowingly awesome event that has ever happened in venture capital," Narasin, founding partner of Tenacity Venture Capital, told CNBC in an interview, adding that he didn't even invest in the company.

    Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO and an additional $26 billion from tech giants that bought at the offer price. The stock gained 17% in its debut on Thursday, lifting Anthropic's market cap to $1.8 trillion and providing a much-needed windfall for Silicon Valley's startup ecosystem.

    In a recent development, it was quite the split-screen moment on Wall Street, which spent the week in an AI-driven tailspin. Led by Nvidia's 23% plunge, which marked the stock's sharpest weekly pullback in 18 years, the Nasdaq slid 10% over the past five trading days in its worst week since the early days of Covid in 2020.

    Investors and analysts spent the week debating whether Anthropic will trade alongside AI hardware, as it's reliant on advanced chips, memory and data centers, or whether it will stand alone as the first public pure-play AI developer and a firm that's achieved unrivaled growth in less than six years of existence.

    It has been revealed that that question will likely persist for some time, but Friday's market action demonstrated that Wall Street is skeptical of Anthropic's ability to grow into its lofty valuation. At week's end, the Claude creator's $1.6 trillion fully diluted market cap put it behind just six U.S. companies: Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Nvidia, Amazon and SpaceX.

    With the tech market in turmoil due to rising interest rates, raging anti-AI sentiment and Nvidia's C-suite crisis, Anthropic's IPO was part exuberance, part relief for an industry hungry for exits.

    Industry observers note that after venture-backed IPOs yielded $73 billion in proceeds in 2021, the amount raised in the next four years totaled just $39 billion, according to data from University of Florida emeritus professor Jay Ritter. In 2021, 126 technology companies went public, compared with 34 in 2025.

    Meanwhile, the private market has continued to balloon, with companies raising ever-larger sums at sky-high valuations without the pressures of quarterly earnings. Many startups that had hoped to go public early in the decade fell out of favor in the AI boom. They experienced hefty job cuts, down rounds and acquisitions for pennies on the dollar.

    Industry observers note that "There was a time in Silicon Valley not that long ago where the prevailing wisdom was the default path should be avoiding going public for as long as possible," noted Somesh Dash, a general partner at venture firm IVP. The view was, "it's too long, it's too hard, it's not worth it," he said.

    It has been revealed that anthropic is very young compared to some of those companies, but it was a huge collector of private capital. Investors poured $141 billion into the AI lab as of September, according to Anthropic's prospectus.

    For a few Silicon Valley firms that contributed to those funding rounds, the returns are unlike anything they've ever seen. At the IPO price, Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners each owned about $25 billion worth of Anthropic stock. Bessemer Venture Partners owned a stake worth roughly $10 billion, partner Byron Deeter said.

    Matt Murphy, a partner at Menlo, told CNBC's David Faber on Thursday that his firm has more than five limited partners "that we delivered over $1 billion of returns to.".

    Sources indicate that "At the end of the day, that's really our job, is to get dollars back into foundations and endowments," Murphy remarked. "There's a lot of pride in being able to do that.".

    Bessemer's Deeter was also jubilant on Thursday, posting on X that, in addition to being "the largest bet in Bessemer's history," the IPO "is a punctuation mark in the history of both humanity and computation.".

    That's quite a change from a few years earlier, when Anthropic was hardly generating revenue, and success was far from guaranteed. In 2023, Anthropic's Claude 2 was struggling to keep pace with models from Google and OpenAI. In April 2024, investors at Bessemer wrote in a memo that if Anthropic missed its own targets, there was "a good chance that we lose all or part of our money.".

    Guru Chahal at Lightspeed told CNBC that Anthropic was clearly the team taking a more measured approach to AI. The company looked beyond Nvidia's dominant AI chips, choosing to use alternatives from Amazon and Google as well. Anthropic remarked it generated $1.72 in revenue per dollar spent on computing power in the third quarter, up from 68 cents a year earlier.

    In a recent development, "It is true that it required lots of capital, but when you dig in and you realize that capital is going toward compute, and this is the team that's positioned to use that compute in the most effective way, then we could connect those dots," Chahal mentioned. He added that those metrics showed it was "going to be a very high-quality business.".

    Anthropic isn't the only substantial win for VCs this year.

    In a recent development, five months before Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, SpaceX hit the market in what, until this week, was by far the largest IPO in history. SpaceX, which Elon Musk founded in 2002, produced outsized returns for firms including Sequoia and Andreessen Horowitz.

    SpaceX and Anthropic alone will make 2026 a monster year for the venture industry, easily exceeding any other year in IPO proceeds. And investors in OpenAI hope appetite remains strong for trillion-dollar companies next year, as the ChatGPT maker is looking to 2027 for a potential offering.

    IVP's Dash stated that in his AI portfolio, "a lot of companies are starting IPO prep" even if it's only "year four, year five, year six since inception." He hopes to see at least half a dozen companies go public at valuations north of $10 billion each in the second half of 2027.

    The macro picture, however, is ominous.

    In a recent development, jensen Huang's sudden departure from Nvidia has left the chip giant without a clear leader at a time when the manufacturer already faced heightened concerns about a slowdown in spending. Nvidia is a key investor in Anthropic and OpenAI and a critical supplier and financing partner for the entire AI industry, which is getting hammered across the board.

    According to recent reports, in January, Democrats will take control of the House and Senate after this month's midterm elections, which included the passage of numerous ballot measures that could stymie data center development. Anthropic investor Brad Gerstner predicted after the election that market dynamics would push Anthropic to price toward the lower end of its range.

    Narasin noted he wasn't even sure the tech giant would get that far.

    "I was concerned they'd delay," Narasin mentioned.

    That makes the outcome that much more impressive, he mentioned, after Anthropic priced above its expected range and upsized the offering.

    Sources indicate that "This will be bedtime stories for years for future VCs," Narasin said. "There was a tech giant that was created, backed by angels and later venture" that in a few short years "became the single biggest IPO of all history.".

    — CNBC's Ari Levy contributed to this report.

    WATCH: I like owning Anthropic over the long term, states Gabelli Funds' John Belton.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the organization "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    Industry observers note that the report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the organization kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also said that upcoming export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    Sources indicate that the allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    Recent findings suggest that "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson stated in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the firm's recent earnings call that China is an "vital" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.
    • The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

    The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

    That goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

    Industry observers note that that confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ upcoming set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

    Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE.

    Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

    And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

    After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

    The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

    It has been revealed that while they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

    For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

    It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

    Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

    In a recent development, had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

    Considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

    Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

    Johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

    There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

    Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

    The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

    That was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

    There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

    Will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

    Sources indicate that mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

    It’s been an entertaining match.

    Recent findings suggest that it’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

    Chelsea have been better this half than the first 45, they’ve been able to control the pace of the game well since the break.

    Recent findings suggest that the pace has slowed down since the break, Chelsea seeing more of the ball. They work it right before Watson loses possession on the edge of the area.

    In a recent development, the referee clearly forgot about the hydration break and the two teams are having a belated one now. Delightful...

    It has been revealed that I reckon there’s another goal left in this match. It’s been entertaining fare and the hosts have given as good as they’ve got, if not more.

    This has been a lively match, better than most run-of-the-mill pre-season friendlies. Chelsea seeing a fair bit of possession at the moment, can they fashion a chance?

    It has been revealed that yes they can. But it’s a longish shot from Gittens that is easily saved by Hamzi in the JDT goal.

    More niggle in this match that hasn’t really had many tough challenges. After a few handbags the referee takes control and the argy bargy peters out.

    Industry observers note that it’s the least the hosts deserve. They have a free-kick 25 yards out, Arribas takes it with his right it’s at the wall but in turning away from the ball Delap deflects it into the far-right corner giving Slonina no chance.

    Fluky goal but the hosts have deserved their bit of luck.

    Delap again with the goal, this time he goes low, but still to the keeper’s right.

    Recent findings suggest that penalty for Chelsea. Gittens cuts back in the box onto his right and is clipped by the defender. Clear-cut penalty.

    It has been revealed that half-chance for Delap on the edge of the area. He playes a one-two with Jackson before opening up his body and letting fly, the shot going well wide.

    Another good chance for the hosts and it’s not shock to write that it’s come from the industry of Arribas on the right. He fires in a low cross that evades everyone in the box.

    Estevao goes down in the box, it looks as though it could well be a penalty but the referee waves play on. The Brazilian is the shown a yellow card for possibly lashing out having not got the decision he wanted.

    The hosts have asserted themselves well this half, in much the same way as they did in the first 45 minutes.

    Another good chance for the hosts and again it’s all too easy as Zahedi is one-on-one with the keeper. The striker, however, dithers a bit too long and Slonina makes a fine save. JDT have had plenty of chances to add to their sole goal...

    Chelsea have had a ragged start to this half.

    Good work from JDT who keep the ball well in midfield before a throughball is played to the on-rushing Zahedi but Slonina comes out well.

    They’re back under way in Johor, and there’s an early chance for Jackson who gets the ball in the box, but the ball gets stuck underneath him and he cannot get in a good attempt in on goal.

    And that is the last action of an entertaining half. Chelsea started well before the hosts opened the scoring. JDT then took control of the half and should, if truth be told, have extended their lead. But Delap did well to earn the penalty that he subsequently scored and should have made it 2-1 with the last kick of the 45.

    Worrying signs at the back, however, for Alonso. Will Chelsea go to four at the back after the break?

    The answer to that question (see last post) was so very nearly yes...

    Industry observers note that jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

    Recent findings suggest that there will be three minutes of added time. Can Chelsea head into the break with an unexpected lead?

    Free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

    A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

    Recent findings suggest that the hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

    Having won the penalty Delap fires the spotkick home, sending the keeper the the wrong way.

    In a recent development, penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

    Chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back presently.

    It has been revealed that as I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

    Industry observers note that JDT are finding a lot of joy on the flanks, there are three at the back for Chelsea and on the outside are two youngsters. The hosts are working the space well.

    In a recent development, yet again Chelsea are made to look decidedly average. A simple ball over the top on the right opens up the visitors’ defence and Arribas is in on goal, he cuts in and lets fly with his left peg, the shot going wide.

    That should have been 2-0 to the Malaysian powerhouses.

    Worrying signs for Chelsea who have struggled to keep possession up top and looked vulnerable at the back.

    Industry observers note that yet more good work from JDT who are being given space by Chelsea. Marcos Guilherme slaloms into the west Londoners’ box and Tosin again doesn’t look the most assured but the JDT player cuts the ball back and the visitors can clear the danger.

    Another good attack from the hosts who get in a shot in on goal, it’s deflected and loops into the grateful arms of Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal.

    There’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

    Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

    Recent findings suggest that yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

    According to recent reports, there’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

    Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

    After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

    Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

    Lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

    In a recent development, so very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

    Recent findings suggest that free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

    What can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

    JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

    No sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

    Quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

    In a recent development, JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

    They’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

    We’re moments away from kick-off.

    CHELSEA XI TO FACE JOHOR: Sharman-Lowe; Sarr, Tosin, Anselmino; Quenda, Nicoll-Jazuli, Essugo (c), Gittens; Estevao; Jackson, Delap; subs: Slonina, Curd, Subuloye, Diakite, Watson, Mudryk, Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen, Satpayev.

    ...Luis Garcia. The Spaniard has history with Chelsea, remember the ‘ghost goal’?

    Arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n.

    It has been revealed that your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc.

    A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

    Industry observers note that johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

    Sources indicate that as if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The fresh season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

    Industry observers note that chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

    A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

    The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

    Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

    Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

    Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

    “The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

    “We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our initiative and we’ve stuck to that.

    “We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”.

    Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

    #73458. How Asian countries are looking to prop up markets as AI downturn sinks stocks

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (618 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    How Asian countries are looking to prop up markets as AI downturn sinks stocks

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (618 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • South Korea, China and Taiwan have introduced fresh measures aimed at supporting their respective markets, as a tech-fueled sell-off in the region spills into another week.
    • On Sunday, South Korea's finance ministry remarked it would prepare its securities-market stabilization fund for immediate activation.
    • Industry observers note that the government also aims to relax listed companies' daily share-buyback order limits for three months, starting Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    South Korea, China and Taiwan have introduced fresh measures aimed at supporting their respective markets, as a tech-fueled sell-off in the region spills into another week.

    On Sunday, South Korea's finance ministry remarked it would prepare its securities-market stabilization fund for immediate activation. The fund, reportedly established in 2020 during the Covid-19 pandemic by financial firms and other institutions seeks to support markets during sharp downturns and is valued at 10.76 trillion won (nearly $8 billion).

    Industry observers note that the government also aims to relax listed companies' daily share-buyback order limits for three months, starting Nov. 24 and start a "special intensive monitoring period" to prevent illegal short-selling. Regulators will also track margin lending and forced liquidations.

    South Korean stocks have seen wild swings over 2026 as investors piled into, then fled from its two tech heavyweights, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, both critical companies in the AI supply chain. The benchmark Kospi index is deep in bear territory, down more than 46% from its June high.

    Industry observers note that the ministry remarked that it "assessed that volatility in domestic and international stock markets has significantly increased recently due to internal and external uncertainties surrounding the global AI and semiconductor industries, as well as U.S. interest rate hikes," according to a Google translation of the release in Korean.

    However, Seoul also said that the mid-to-long-term growth expectations for the AI industry remain intact, and that "excessive anxiety is not a concern.".

    Taiwan, which is also exposed to the AI industry through Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and other tech firms, has also moved to rein in market volatility.

    Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission unveiled Friday that short selling below the closing price was "completely prohibited," while making it an exception if used for hedging purposes by securities and futures firms.

    "Investors must not sell listed (OTC) stocks or Taiwan Depositary Receipts at a price lower than the closing price of the previous trading day," the FSC stated, according to a Google translation of the statement in Chinese.

    Margin requirements for short selling will also be increased, and applications from securities firms to matter warrants for listing will be suspended, as the regulator aims to curb speculative activity.

    In a similar move to Seoul, Taipei encouraged firms to buy back stocks, adding that the purchases will be included in the companies' environmental, social and governance scores if completed between the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2027.

    It has been revealed that the island's stock market is heavily dominated by its tech industry, most notably, chip manufacturing giant TSMC. The stock fell 15% last week, while the index dropped 17.5%.

    While South Korea and Taiwan are looking to curb speculative trading to arrest the slide in their markets, Beijing is looking to encourage more leverage-based buying.

    The Shanghai Stock Exchange stated on Sunday that exchanges in Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing will cut the minimum margin ratio for margin-financed stock purchases to 80% from 100%, starting Nov. 30. That means investors will be able to borrow more for their stock market bets.

    The Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges also announced fee cuts, while Shenzhen proposed a market-making mechanism for its ChiNext board. The steps will help inject more liquidity into the market that has also born the brunt of the souring in tech and AI trade, with the benchmark CSI 300 index closing lower for 14 of the past 15 weeks.

    Industry observers note that seoul's markets led losses in the region, with the Kospi down over 3.26%. Smaller losses were seen in mainland China's CSI 300, which declined 0.71%. The Taiwan Weighted Index, however, reversed earlier losses to gain over 2% on Monday.

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns Americans of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road" after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook.
    • Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.
    • Clayton, however, noted on CNN's "State of the Union" that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road" after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook.

    Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.

    Clayton, however, noted on CNN's "State of the Union" that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age.

    "The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road," Clayton mentioned.

    "You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot," he mentioned.

    According to recent reports, clayton's warning came as the U.S. prepares to celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday, one of the busiest travel weeks of the year. A technology outage prompted a nationwide ground stop just over a week ago, which lasted for hours.

    The Federal Aviation Administration said router upgrades caused a flood of data that led to the ground stop, and that there is no indication of a cyberattack.

    Separately, Microsoft stated the Outlook outage was caused by "an glitch during an earlier network capacity upgrade.".

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message on CBS' "Face the Nation.".

    Asked if Americans should be concerned about the security of their financial institutions, Bessent remarked: "No, they shouldn't.".

    Sources indicate that "The patches may cause a glitch," he said, referring to measures banks are taking to safeguard from AI. "I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency.".

    Latest Update: Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a significant win for the tech giant and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    According to recent reports, some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    According to recent reports, adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and said it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the massive indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he stated.

    Part of the challenge, Niles noted, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," mentioned JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he noted, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan said. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the company in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    Recent findings suggest that "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he stated. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    According to recent reports, one bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton stated the U.S. is investigating Alice Huang and her former company, Megaspeed, as a report identified one of her associates as a key decision-maker at the Singapore-based company.

    Alice Huang, with whom ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly had a romantic relationship, was a key figure in Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia linked to the fallout surrounding the leadership shake-up.

    According to recent reports, "There is an investigation ongoing into her firm and into her," Clayton told ABC on Sunday, adding that, "Nvidia chips, they are the jewel. They are the absolute top that everybody wants, that's why we're focusing on this.".

    Alice Huang's associate, Chinese national Li Ming, who is now out on bail in Singapore, was "deeply involved" in Megaspeed's activities and took part in major decisions, The Wall Street Journal reported earlier on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.

    The Singapore charges against Li concern alleged false representations to Super Micro Computer, a U.S.-based firm with known links to chipmaker Nvidia, though Megaspeed is not named in those charges.

    Recent findings suggest that last week, the Commerce and Justice departments said that the investigation into Megaspeed began in 2024 over potential export-control violations. Their joint statement said Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security and Singapore law enforcement interviewed Huang during an on-site check in June 2025.

    The Justice Department later took the lead in the criminal investigation.

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CBS on Sunday that the administration was seeking answers from Nvidia about its chip sales to China, including who oversaw compliance and which levels of the manufacturer knew about the activity.

    In a recent development, separately, The Latest York Times reported Sunday that Alice Huang was in contact with an officer of a top Chinese intelligence agency from spring 2025 through fall 2026, citing people briefed on U.S. intelligence reports.

    Bloomberg reported last week that the Justice Department is investigating whether entities linked to Alice Huang helped smuggle Super Micro products to China.

    Li faces five charges in Singapore, including two counts of fraud by false representation, along with allegations involving the operation of a company he controlled, unauthorized bank-account access and another company director's duties.

    Prosecutors allege he falsely told Super Micro that the company would hold and lease the servers it purchased.

    In a recent development, the Journal reported that Li is out on bail and that his case is ongoing. He was offered bail of S$1 million in March 2025. The Singapore charges do not name Megaspeed.

    Earlier this month, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs mentioned that police had found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang committed offenses related to the possible inaccurate declarations under investigation.

    The ministry said she was issued a stern warning for providing information that police assessed as knowingly inaccurate and for downplaying her role at Megaspeed. It also said Singapore had not investigated her for espionage.

    Megaspeed has said it is a "legitimate and lawful business" and that Huang left the company in August 2025.

    The scrutiny is set to intensify in Washington. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and the company's general counsel, Tim Teter, have agreed to closed-door, transcribed interviews with three House committees on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2, respectively.

    The committees said they want answers about Nvidia's role in allowing Chinese actors to access advanced chips and the involvement of a potential Chinese intelligence asset.

    It has been revealed that speaking to CNBC's Squawk Box on Sunday U.S. time, Ryan Fedasiuk, a former advisor for U.S.-China Bilateral Affairs at the State Department, mentioned that there was "still a lot we don't know" about the case.

    He said lawmakers would likely focus on Nvidia's customer relationships and "who knew what at the company when.".

    According to recent reports, fedasiuk added that there was "a very good chance" investigators would find that people at Nvidia knew their products could be used for restricted purposes. He characterized the existing evidence as containing "multiple" smoking guns.

    It has been revealed that yemen's Houthis, backed by Iran, said Sunday that they had targeted Rabigh oil refinery in Saudi Arabia, in the latest sign of worsening hostilities in the region, as Iranian forces seek to pressure the U.S. into accepting its terms.

    The Houthis mentioned they has directly hit the infrastructure, though the extent of the damage remains unclear, Reuters reported.

    The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis noted earlier in the day that it had "intercepted and destroyed" a drone launched by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia's western region, which included some of the country's critical energy refining and export infrastructure.

    Rabigh, about 165 kilometers north of Jeddah on the kingdom's western Red Sea coast, hosts Petro Rabigh, a major oil refining and petrochemical complex, developed by Saudi Aramco and Japan's Sumitomo Chemical.

    Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Interior did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.

    Gulf countries reported multiple attacks by Iran-linked forces over the weekend, even as the country's foreign minister said his government remains open to a negotiated end to the war. Bahrain authorities said an Iranian attack on a civilian industrial facility injured two people on Saturday.

    The string of attacks mark the latest sign of escalation in the regional hostilities since the war between the U.S.-Israel and Iran began in late February, as negotiators have so far failed to agree on terms to end the monthslong war.

    The conflict has drawn in countries in the Gulf region, disrupting energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, which used to carry a fifth of the world's crude shipments prior to the war, pushing up global prices for oil and commodities.

    Sources indicate that the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported another incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday, after two tankers were struck by unknown projectiles the day before. The maritime agency gave no further details about the incident, urging vessels to stay vigilant about the operational environment.

    In a recent development, tehran has indicated its intention to end the war with the U.S. through diplomacy, but President Donald Trump has dismissed Iranian proposals. Both sides have been in indirect communication via Qatar.

    In an interview to Fox News on Saturday, Trump warned that he was inclined to order military strikes against Tehran next year, if the two countries failed to finalize an agreement. The president blamed the Iranian officials for stalling while escalating hostilities after the U.S. elections.

    "They're more aggressive now than before the election," Trump stated, describing Iranian officials as "professional tap dancers." "They talk all the time, all they do is talk," he added.

    The president has previously noted that Tehran wants a deal to end hostilities but not one that is "acceptable" to him. He has oscillated between favoring an agreement that would end the fighting and insisting that the U.S. does not need to rush into any deal and is not afraid of resuming more aggressive attacks.

    The Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Saturday after a two-hour meeting with visiting Qatari mediators that, "We are in contact with mediators, including the Qataris, both in person and virtually, and are holding the necessary discussions to see whether another opportunity can be given to diplomacy," according to Reuters.

    International benchmark Brent futures inched 0.22% lower to $92.35 per barrel in early Asia trading hours, while WTI crude was down 0.19% at $83.25 a barrel.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence firm in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • Industry observers note that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence firm in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    Industry observers note that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    Sources indicate that anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    Sources indicate that "We're climbing a wall of worry," said Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, new technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    It has been revealed that the Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood said she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    According to recent reports, in her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    In a recent development, ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the significant losses.

    The fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she stated. "That's how crazy things were.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot at the moment “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

    In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

    Recent findings suggest that “We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

    “We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”.

    Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

    Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

    A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

    Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

    Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw.

    It has been revealed that at that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

    Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

    According to recent reports, cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

    Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré. Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88).

    They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

    Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

    Recent findings suggest that liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

    Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

    Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

    The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺.

    Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

    This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under latest management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

    In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

    Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

    Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

    As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • Sources indicate that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    It has been revealed that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    Sources indicate that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the latest tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Sources indicate that implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders substantial and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," stated Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    Vikings' defense has first poor outing of season as 49ers dominate in easy win
