    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the Minnesota Vikings had high hopes after last week, when Kirk Cousins joined the team and they blew out the Green Bay Packers.
    • Sunday night was a good time to measure where the Vikings stood in the NFC hierarchy.
    • The 49ers have looked like a Super Bowl contender since Week 1 when they blew out the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, and that domination continued in Mexico City on Sunday night.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the Minnesota Vikings had high hopes after last week, when Kirk Cousins joined the team and they blew out the Green Bay Packers. With the Vikings' defense playing very well yet again and Cousins providing much better play at quarterback in his first game with Minnesota after coming over in a trade, entering the Super Bowl discussion seemed reasonable.

    Sunday night was a good time to measure where the Vikings stood in the NFC hierarchy. And they found out there's a big gap between them and the San Francisco 49ers.

    The 49ers have looked like a Super Bowl contender since Week 1 when they blew out the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, and that domination continued in Mexico City on Sunday night. The 49ers handled the Vikings with surprising ease. They improved to 9-1 with a 35-10 win.

    The Vikings (7-3) are still in good shape. But their defense finally demonstrated some vulnerability and their offense took a step back from the first game with Cousins. Minnesota could still win the NFC North and make a deep playoff run, but Sunday showed there's a long way to go to reach the 49ers' level.

    Kirk Cousins of the Minnesota Vikings is hit by Nick Bosa of the San Francisco 49ers.

    The Vikings' defense was in trouble from the first drive. The 49ers moved the ball without any problem downfield and then tight end George Kittle scored on a 17-yard touchdown. The ease in which the 49ers moved the ball was surprising because nobody had been able to move it like that on the Vikings. The Vikings were so dominant, they held the Bears and their explosive offense to three points in Week 2. But the Vikings had no answers for the 49ers.

    Coordinator Brian Flores brings extra pass rushers way more than any other defense in the NFL, and once the 49ers figured out how to combat that by Brock Purdy getting the ball out swiftly, Minnesota's defense wasn't so scary anymore.

    The 49ers scored touchdowns on three of their first four drives. Minnesota hadn't allowed more than 23 points in a game all season and the 49ers had 21 before halftime when Mike Evans made a great catch in the end zone, though there was a question if he had control with both feet down. It didn't matter because the touchdown call stood and at that point the Vikings were in danger of the game slipping away.

    Then Cousins made a mistake before halftime that practically finished the game before halftime.

    The Vikings trailed 21-10 when 49ers safety Ji'Ayir Brown read Cousins and the Vikings' play perfectly and jumped in front of a pass intended for Tai Felton. Brown picked it off and had an easy 18-yard return for the touchdown.

    Minnesota's defense having its troubles with Purdy and the 49ers was the key to the game but the Vikings' offense struggled too. They got a touchdown in the first quarter and didn't get another the rest of the game.

    Industry observers note that the Vikings are known for pressuring quarterbacks, but it was the 49ers who had constant pressure on Cousins. NBC's cameras found Cousins in an animated discussion with tackle Brian O'Neill on the sideline, seemingly telling O'Neill he was being hit every play. Without much of a running game or protection on pass plays, it was tough for Cousins to function.

    Sources indicate that the Vikings are still one of the NFL's better teams. They just had a tough matchup against a 49ers team that has a great argument as the best in the NFL. There's a long way to go in the season. That gives Minnesota time to figure out how it can match up better with San Francisco the next time, if they happen to meet in the playoffs.

    According to recent reports, and we're officially done in Mexico City. The 49ers are now a near-perfect 9-1 after the win, which marked their third straight.

    In a recent development, the Vikings hold a 7-3 record, and have lost three of their last four. They are 1-1 now with Kirk Cousins as a starter after the deadline trade.

    Carson Wentz is in for the Vikings now, and Brock Purdy's day is done, too, as we hit the two mintue warning.

    The 49ers couldn't extend their drive to kill the game here, and got stopped on third after Deebo Samuel was stopped a few yards short of the first.

    Minnesota will take back over with 3:46 to go, but this one is over.

    The Vikings got all the way to the SF 20, but their attempt on fourth down was stopped just a few yards short of the line to gain.

    They needed a touchdown there to stay alive. Instead, Kirk Cousins is headed back to the sidelines down by 25 with just 8:16 to go.

    Recent findings suggest that and that should do it. Christian McCaffery punched in a 6-yard score one play after making his first catch of the night, and the 49ers are now up 35-10.

    That was a 98 yard drive for San Francisco.

    It was a scoreless third period, but San Francisco is knocking on the red zone looking to extend its lead.

    If they can add seven more here, this game will essentially be over. The Vikings absolutely need a stop.

    In a recent development, the 49ers were all over Tai Felton there to break up the pass, and the Vikings will now have to punt. That was a long 10-play drive, but htey only made it 36 yards before having to punt.

    Minnesota will have to get points on the board here soon if it's going to mount a comeback.

    The Vikings defense has responded yet again. They forced a quck three-and-out, and put too much pressure on Brock Purdy in the backfield there on third down for him to get a good throw off.

    Minnesota will get another shot with the ball here in the second half.

    Industry observers note that justin Jefferson looked like he had a path to the end zone there, but he did not have a firm grip on the ball at all. Deommodore Lenoir easily punched the ball out of his hands to force the early turnover.

    San Francisco has suddenly taken back over. That's not the start Minnesota needed.

    Industry observers note that the Vikings have received the kick, and the second half is underway. We'll see if they can rally here.

    It has been revealed that the 49ers weren't able to score there, but they've been dominating so far tonight in Mexico City. Brock Purdy has thrown for 176 yards and three touchdowns already, two of which went to George Kittle.

    Minnesota will get the ball to start the second half. The Vikings attempted a 71-yard field goal just before half, but it was just barely short. That was only the 10th 70+ yard attempt in NFL history.

    Sources indicate that san Francisco will have a chance to put up more points before half. The 49ers forced a quick three-and-out there, so the Vikings will have to put with 68 seconds left before the break.

    One more touchdown before half would blow this game wide open.

    Industry observers note that what a turn for the 49ers! On the first play after Mike Evans' touchdown, Ji'Ayir Brown jumped up and intercepted Kirk Cousins to set up an easy trot into the end zone.

    All of the sudden, their lead is 28-10.

    What a grab from Mike Evans! Brock Purdy found him in the back corner, and he hauled that ball in with just one hand perfectly.

    The 49ers lead 21-10 now with 2:09 left in the half.

    Colton McKivitz went down with what appears to be a significant ankle injury. His ankle was going off the wrong direction, and teammate Trent Williams slammed his helmet there after seeing it up close.

    He's being carted off now, and the entire 49ers team came over to see him off.

    The Vikings had to settle for a 48-yard field goal there after their drive stalled out. They converted on fourth-and-short earlier to keep it alive, too.

    Sources indicate that but points are points. The 49ers lead 14-10 now with 6:48 left in the half.

    Recent findings suggest that george Kittle had to power through Harrison Smith to make the grab, but he's now got his second touchdown of the night. What a catch.

    The 49ers lead 14-7 now early in the second.

    Recent findings suggest that we're all tied up after the first quarter in Mexico City, but the 49ers are driving once again. Brock Purdy just found Mike Evans for a 34-yard gain right up the middle, and they're in the red zone.

    In a recent development, just like that, the Vikings have tied this game up. Aaron Jones capped the nine-play drive with an 11-yard touchdown run up the left side.

    Nick Bosa nearly got his first sack of the season on Kirk Cousins on the play right before the score, too. But instead, he was hit with a penalty for drilling Cousins in the backfield.

    It's 7-7 now with 1:13 left in the first.

    Prediction markets outlook for stocks in 2026 dims amid AI sell-off

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (267 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.
    • On platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026.
    • Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    On platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    According to recent reports, on Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note stated.

    Industry observers note that the Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    Sources indicate that in that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.
    • The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.
    • Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

    The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

    Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

    In a recent development, but enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

    The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

    According to recent reports, ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

    Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

    Sources indicate that arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

    As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

    Champions 🏆 pic.twitter.com/c0IVLYu3fB.

    Sources indicate that arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

    It has been revealed that another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

    Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

    Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

    Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

    Industry observers note that arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

    The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

    There will now be a penalty shootout.

    It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

    There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

    Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

    Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:.

    In a recent development, with just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

    It has been revealed that the Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

    Sources indicate that tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

    It has been revealed that nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

    Industry observers note that in the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

    Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

    Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

    In a recent development, should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

    In a recent development, mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

    Sources indicate that that is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

    Industry observers note that white is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

    Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

    According to recent reports, dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

    The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

    Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

    After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

    Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

    Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

    In a recent development, with it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

    It has been revealed that what a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

    Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

    Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

    A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

    In a recent development, down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

    Sources indicate that odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

    Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,.

    According to recent reports, dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal challenges and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

    Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

    It has been revealed that arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

    Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀.

    When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

    The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

    Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

    Recent findings suggest that yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:.

    “I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a newly introduced challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

    “I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very key and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”.

    In a recent development, premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the upcoming season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

    Industry observers note that arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

    Recent findings suggest that “I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

    According to recent reports, “I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”.

    It has been revealed that this is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

    Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz left Sunday's dominant win over the Minnesota Vikings due to what looked like a significant injury to his lower left leg.
    • The injury took place during the second quarter of the 35-10 win that was held in Mexico City.
    • When McKivitz pulled his leg from underneath the pile of players, his foot was twisted in the wrong direction.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz left Sunday's dominant win over the Minnesota Vikings due to what looked like a significant injury to his lower left leg.

    The injury took place during the second quarter of the 35-10 win that was held in Mexico City. McKivitz's left leg got pinned under multiple players at the end of a Christian McCaffrey run.

    When McKivitz pulled his leg from underneath the pile of players, his foot was twisted in the wrong direction.

    Warning: Video below shows a graphic injury.

    According to recent reports, mcKivitz's teammates immediately knew he had sustained a significant injury. Multiple players took a knee around their injured teammate, and left tackle Trent Williams slammed his helmet into the turf, then held the back of his head in his hands.

    Trainers rushed onto the field to tend to McKivitz. He was eventually taken off the field on a cart. He was upright and interacting with his teammates as they saw him off the field.

    The nature of McKivitz's injury wasn't initially clear.

    McKivitz is key to San Francisco's top-ranked offense. He's a strong run blocker who hasn't allowed a sack this season.

    In a recent development, the 49ers have thrived despite injuries to key players on both sides of the ball this season, and Sunday night was no exception. They entered halftime with a 28-10 lead and cruised the rest of the way to secure the 25-point win. Brock Purdy went 21-of-26 for 255 yards with three touchdowns, two of which went to George Kittle.

    They now sit at 9-1 on the season after the win, which marked their third straight.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I asked Claude after Friday's close what I should do about the tanking stock market.
    • It has been revealed that amazon's cloud business is growing at its fastest pace in nearly five years.
    • It has been revealed that AWS demand supports the lower end of the range.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I asked Claude after Friday's close what I should do about the tanking stock market. Its advice was surprisingly useful: avoid panic selling and look for opportunities. A 40 VIX, which it touched Friday, might provide those opportunities. Specifically, a higher VIX (higher options premiums) signals fear, but it also creates an opportunity to sell elevated premium in some premium stocks, like Amazon.

    It has been revealed that amazon's cloud business is growing at its fastest pace in nearly five years. AWS revenue rose 39.3% YoY in the third quarter, and management reported a $578 billion backlog. Trailing 12-month operating cash flow rose 29% to $168.3 billion. However, infrastructure investment accelerated, resulting in more than $42 billion in negative cash flow. The competing forces of accelerating growth and the cost of supplying it could keep the stock in its range over the next four weeks. Its shares are only off 14% from its recent highs, comparatively better than the Nasdaq Composite's near 19% decline.

    It has been revealed that AWS demand supports the lower end of the range. The backlog gives Amazon a basis for adding capacity even as investors scrutinize the cash cost. Cash spending could temper an upside rerating.

    The next leg higher may require evidence that new capacity can earn attractive returns at this scale, and that evidence may be in short supply over the next couple of months.

    Sources indicate that sell the Dec. 18, 2026 AMZN 235/285 strangle for an indicative $5.90 credit per share.

    Max reward — $590 per strangle if AMZN finishes between $235 and $285 at expiration, before fees.

    Breakevens at expiration — $229.10 and $290.90.

    Max risk — Unlimited on the uncovered call, but one should think of the trade as risking getting short at a net price above $290, a nearly 13% premium to today's closing price. The downside loss would reach $22,910 per strangle if AMZN fell to zero. The credit is roughly 2.3% of a $260 reference share price over four weeks, or nearly 30% on a simple annualized basis. That comparison uses the share price as its denominator. Actual return on capital depends on margin and the cost to close or settle the trade.

    Industry observers note that buying in bear markets, as the Nasdaq just touched, is never easy. But those opportunities don't present themselves too often. What are you going to do with it?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Investors often favor dividend stocks for their regular income and the promise of potential share price appreciation. But selecting the right dividend stocks from a huge pool of companies can be difficult.

    Top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend-paying stocks, as their recommendations are backed by thorough analysis of a company's financials.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Recent findings suggest that devon Energy (DVN), an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company, reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. The company revealed a quarterly dividend of 32 cents per share for the fourth quarter, payable December 30. Based on the fixed dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, DVN yields 2.85%.

    Recent findings suggest that after hosting a virtual investor meeting with management, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Devon, with a price target of $59. Mehta mentioned that he is now more confident in management's outlook for delivering strong near-term capital returns as well as efforts to drive operational efficiencies and productivity gains.

    Devon sees an opportunity to increase share repurchases, driven by solid free cash flow (FCF), contributions from the Eagle Ford divestiture and continued improvement in the balance sheet, Mehta noted. Devon expects share buybacks worth more than $1 billion in Q4 2026, up from $414 million in the third quarter, backed by a strong pricing backdrop and improved capital efficiency.

    Mehta, a 5-star analyst, said Devon expects about $6.3 billion of excess FCF in 2027, including about $3.5 billion of net proceeds from the Eagle Ford sale. That would enable the organization to accelerate buybacks while progressing toward its goal of reducing gross debt to about $9 billion by early 2027. Mehta noted that under DVN's framework to return up to 70% of annual FCF, management favors share buybacks as it believes the stock is discounted compared to large-cap peers.

    "Management expects continued capital efficiency gains from merger synergies, extended laterals, surfactant adoption and development of the newly acquired federal acreage," Mehta said.

    In a recent development, mehta ranks No. 876 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.1%. See Devon Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that energy Transfer (ET), is a limited partnership that operates about 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. The company recently announced third-quarter results showing net income per common unit growing about 18% year-over-year, to 33 cents. ET's cash distribution for Q3 2026 was 34.25 cents per common unit, up more than 3% year-over-year. At an annualized distribution of $1.37 per share, Energy Transfer yields more than 7%.

    In a recent development, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer with a price target of $25. The manufacturer delivered better-than-expected Q3 results and declared the 1.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d) South Mississippi Pipeline, a 215-mile, 36-inch natural gas line linking the Perryville Hub to the Florida Gas Transmission (FGT) network, Gabelman noted. The project is supported by 20-year firm transportation agreements and is expected to enter service in 2030. ET expects to ultimately own 51% of the $1.6 billion project.

    The 5-star analyst said that Energy Transfer lowered its 2026 capital spending outlook to $5.5 billion (midpoint of the guidance range) from $5.75 billion due to project timing. Energy Transfer expects capex to rise to $7 billion in 2027, while Gabelman projects $5 billion in both 2028 and 2029, based on disclosed projects.

    Gabelman also highlighted management's commentary about optimization initiatives contributing an incremental $800 million to 2026 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, a larger benefit than in recent years. "A return to less commodity volatility should the [Middle East] war end could bring some relative downside, though this is offset by continued strong growth prospects," he remarked.

    It has been revealed that gabelman ranks No. 397 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15.4%. See Energy Transfer KPIs on TipRanks.

    Oil and gas exploration and production company ConocoPhillips (COP) delivered better-than-expected Q3 performance. The company announced an 11% hike in its quarterly dividend to 93 cents per share, effective with the Q4 dividend payable on December 1. Based on the dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, COP yields about 2.6%.

    It has been revealed that following the Q3 results, Wells Fargo analyst Sam Margolin repeated a buy rating on ConocoPhillips, citing strong potential for further dividend increases. Margolin also trimmed his price target to $185 from $189 to reflect timing effects and the WAHA forward curve, though he noted that COP could still re-rate as its natural portfolio lifecycle provides stronger protection against inflationary pressures than peers. The Waha forward curve tracks future natural gas prices based on the West Texas Waha hub.

    Industry observers note that margolin, another 5-star analyst, highlighted that ConocoPhillips' Q3 2026 adjusted earnings per share of $3.27 was well above Wells Fargo and the Street's estimates of $3.04 and $3.05, respectively. Earnings were driven by solid price realizations, partially offset by higher depletion, depreciation and amortization and purchased commodities.

    Recent findings suggest that margolin also noted COP's dividend increase and said the accelerated buyback enabled by current commodity prices could further support long-term dividend growth. He sees the possibility of ConocoPhillips' dividend growth rate exceeding its current 6% cost of equity into the end of the decade. Margolin expects COP to sustain an 8% dividend compound annual growth rate through 2029 while repurchasing $6.4 billion of stock annually, and reducing net debt-to-capital to less than 9% by the end of 2028 based on the assumption of an average Brent crude oil price of $75 a barrel.

    "The message on the 3Q call was similar to that of 2Q, reiterating the moderation in reinvestment rate and commitment to dividend growth through the Willow start-up and after," Margolin stated.

    Margolin ranks No. 189 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 69% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.6%. See ConocoPhillips Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

    📅 12 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2200 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the latest Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.
    • On a sobering evening for latest Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.
    • Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the latest Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

    On a sobering evening for latest Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

    Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

    Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

    Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

    They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

    Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

    The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

    Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

    Everton kick-off their fresh season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

    The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the upcoming season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

    Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

    Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

    Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

    Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

    More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

    Recent findings suggest that that goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

    Sources indicate that if I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

    Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

    Recent findings suggest that newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

    Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

    Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

    Sources indicate that thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

    Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

    Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

    In a recent development, then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

    It has been revealed that everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

    The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

    He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

    The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

    It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

    Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

    It has been revealed that everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

    Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

    Recent findings suggest that A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

    The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

    This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

    It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

    A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

    Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

    According to recent reports, osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

    Recent findings suggest that good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

    Recent findings suggest that thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

    Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

    Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

    Newcastle get the game under way.

    Industry observers note that bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

    We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

    Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry.

    According to recent reports, here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl.

    Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

    Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

    Industry observers note that “It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle stated.

    According to recent reports, “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

    Sources indicate that “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

    The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

    He remained tight-lipped about newly introduced signings.

    In a recent development, “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

    It has been revealed that “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

    Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

    It has been revealed that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

    “The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Tennessee Titans may have allowed 51 points on Sunday afternoon, but they are still in control of the No. 1 overall pick in 2027 NFL Draft.

    The Titans fell to 1-9 on the season on Sunday afternoon in a rough 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. That marked their fourth straight loss. And, as the Titans hold the key strength of schedule tiebreak, the franchise kept control of the first overall pick in the draft next spring.

    According to recent reports, the Titans overtook the Los Angeles Chargers last week for the top spot after the Chargers finally picked up their first win of the season. But on Sunday, after the Chargers fell to the New York Jets 27-24, they joined the Titans at 1-9 on the year. The Miami Dolphins have just a single win to their name, too. The Buffalo Bills rolled over the Dolphins 26-9 on Sunday, marking the team's fourth-straight loss. But the Chargers' loss kept the Dolphins down at the No. 3 overall pick.

    The Jets now sit at 3-8 on the season. They hold three first-round draft picks in 2027, too, one from the Indianapolis Colts and another from the Cowboys. As things at the moment stand, the Jets will have both the No. 4 and No. 5 picks.

    Now, Week 11 of the season isn't over yet. The Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders will close things out on Monday night in Maryland. And with three teams at 1-9, the race for the No. 1 pick still has a long way to go.

    For now, the Titans are still in control at the top.

    The future of Virgil van Dijk continues to be a much-discussed talking point going into the winter months.

    The legendary Liverpool captain will see his current contract expire next June as things stand, with the Dutchman on track to become a free agent just before his 36th birthday.

    Transfer insider Graeme Bailey recently claimed that there’s a strong chance of the veteran defender being offered at least a 12-month extension at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola unsurprisingly keen to keep hold of his skipper.

    In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele reported of fervent interest from Serie A in Van Dijk amid ongoing speculation over the centre-back’s future.

    The journalist wrote: ‘One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides.

    ‘Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are said to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.’.

    While the Rossoneri appear determined to pounce on any uncertainty over Van Dijk’s future, Steele added that the 35-year-old is ‘keen’ to extend his contract at Liverpool.

    (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images).

    Industry observers note that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Any reports of interest in the Dutchman from other clubs will naturally trigger a level of concern among Reds supporters, but it’s natural that there’d be a queue of suitors for one of the best defenders of his (perhaps any) generation when he’s seven months away from becoming a free agent.

    Recent findings suggest that until such time that a final decision is communicated by LFC, fans’ nerves will be frayed as to Van Dijk’s future. When we’ve already seen Mo Salah and Andy Robertson depart this year, the loss of another modern-day great in 2027 would represent a further gut punch for Kopites.

    However, it’s worth remembering that when the Liverpool captain last penned a upcoming contract in April 2025, he was just over two months away from leaving on a free, so he won’t panic even if there might be considerable gnashing of teeth outside of those involved in negotiations over his future.

    James Pearce recently advised Reds supporters not to expect a ‘quick resolution’ over the defender’s situation, so for now, it seems that the best way for Van Dijk to secure a upcoming deal at Anfield is to maintain the strong performance levels he’s shown so far this season.

    The noise over his future is sure to continue for the time being, but we remain confident that everything will come together in due course and that our iconic number 4 will continue to grace the famous red shirt in the 2027/28 campaign.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

    It has been revealed that emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the major positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

    Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

    Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the fresh year.

    Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

    In a recent development, “Of course there is still work to do but they indicated they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

    It has been revealed that this was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition.     Recent findings suggest that what will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

    In a recent development, unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

    I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

    The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

    In a recent development, aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

    “I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

    Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

    Sources indicate that PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

    Industry observers note that “I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

    According to recent reports, “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

    PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

    #73381. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

    📅 13 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 20m • 📚 Deep Dive (4075 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

    📅 13 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4075 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events?
    • There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.
    • Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

    There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

    Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

    You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

    It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes indicated he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

    Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

    Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

    According to recent reports, the one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward swiftly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

    The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

    It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

    Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

    Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

    There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

    You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

    Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

    He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

    It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

    Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

    Sources indicate that the misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

    Recent findings suggest that good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

    It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

    Recent findings suggest that this one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in Fresh Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

    While Leeds will have fresh signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

    Breaking: Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

    📅 14 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5398 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.
    • Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.
    • According to recent reports, the visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

    Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

    According to recent reports, the visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

    LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

    Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

    Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

    “We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

    In a recent development, “We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”.

    Sources indicate that tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

    In a recent development, mowbray mentioned: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

    According to recent reports, “Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we indicated there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”.

    The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

    However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

    "A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

    Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

    The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

    Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

    "It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

    Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

    However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

    Wolverhampton: Bentley, Trippier, Mosquera, Toti Gomes, Wolfe, Lopez, Andre Trindade, Munetsi, Rodrigo Gomes, Armstrong, Mane.Subs used: Jiménez 60 (Mateus Mané), ‌Doyle ‌67 (Rodrigo Gomes), ⁠Tchatchoua 67 (Trippier), Pedro Lima 79 (André),Chirewa 79 (Møller Wolfe)Scorers: M. Munetsi 18, R. Jiménez 90+3penYellow card: Mateus Mané 52Blackburn: Toth, Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering, Montgomery, Forshaw, Morishita, Cantwell, Afolayan, Gudjohnsen.Subs used: Sam Morsy 55 (Forshaw), Fevrier 68 (Afolayan), Ohashi ‌68 (Cantwell), Garrett ​79 (Gudjohnsen), ⁠Yuri Ribeiro79 (Morishita)Scorers: ⁠S. McLoughlin 27, A. Gudjohnsen 48Yellow card: Pickering ​34, Cantwell 35, ‌Forshaw 45Attendance: 30,984Referee: Farai ⁠Hallam.

    “I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a significant call.”.

    “We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”.

    “It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is important. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”.

    “Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”.

    Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc.

    “Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case. Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”.

    “Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”.

    Saturday:Bolton vs PrestonBristol City vs MillwallCharlton vs DerbyMiddlesbrough vs LincolnNorwich vs West BromPortsmouth vs QPRStoke vs SwanseaSheffield United vs Birmingham.

    Sunday:Watford vs SouthamptonBurnley vs West Ham.
