    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil.
    • Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
    • Sources indicate that hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Latest Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams revealed the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

    Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He mentioned at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

    Sources indicate that hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, Newly introduced Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a fresh era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    Goaltending has been an concern in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a significant reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    Industry observers note that in the early portion of this season, it was clear that Fresh Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    Sources indicate that hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    According to recent reports, although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but Fresh Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    It has been revealed that if we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in Fresh Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    According to recent reports, let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    Recent findings suggest that that remarked, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    Recent findings suggest that the addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    Recent findings suggest that daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For millennia, philosophers and professors have pondered an impossible question: What happens when an irresistible force meets an immovable object?

    • Recent findings suggest that the 49ers strode onto the field at Estadio Azteca and proceeded to stomp all over the Vikings.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    For millennia, philosophers and professors have pondered an impossible question: What happens when an irresistible force meets an immovable object? Well, we have our answer, and we didn't even need AI to solve it: Irresistible Force knocks out Immovable Object by 25 points.

    San Francisco and Minnesota arrived in Mexico City at the absolute pinnacles of the NFL's two barometers of excellence. No team in the NFL gains more yards per play than the 49ers. No team sacks quarterbacks more than Minnesota. Dominating offense, smothering defense. Irresistible force, immovable object.

    Recent findings suggest that the 49ers strode onto the field at Estadio Azteca and proceeded to stomp all over the Vikings. San Francisco set the tone with a seven-play, 72-yard opening drive that finished in the end zone in less than four minutes. The Vikings immediately struck back with a touchdown.

    It has been revealed that and then, like a street fighter wiping a drop of blood off his lip before administering a generational beatdown, the 49ers blew away the league's top scoring defense with a total of 35 points, through the air and on the ground. And if you could score touchdowns by water, well, the 49ers probably would have done that too. This was a statement win carved into the side of a mountain, a declaration that the road to the Super Bowl runs through San Francisco.

    Sources indicate that at 9-1, the 49ers lead the the NFC West by three games and the NFC as a whole by a game, and stand even with the Bills for the best record in the NFL. Aside from an inexplicable loss to the Falcons — who probably won't get another shot at the 49ers this season — San Francisco has overwhelmed its opposition at every turn.

    According to recent reports, if there's anything that can slow this 49ers team, it's the blue medical tent. Injuries have ravaged the 49ers all season, and on Sunday night, San Francisco ran out a Geriatric Avengers of thirty-somethings including George Kittle, Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Kyle Juszczyk. All that experience gives the 49ers a substantial-game-pressure edge that few teams can match, but it also makes them intensely vulnerable to injury. Stints on the IR are a when, not an if, for the 49ers. Right tackle Colton McKivitz was the latest as he suffered a gruesome leg injury in the first half Sunday night.

    In a recent development, the guy ensuring all those uncs get the ball is finally receiving some attention of his own again, too. Brock Purdy hasn't shown up on MVP leaderboards since finishing fourth in his breakout season of 2023. This season ought to change that. He's among the league leaders in touchdowns, passer rating and completion percentage, among other useful stats.

    Against the best defense in the NFL, all Purdy did was throw for three touchdowns and 255 yards on 21-of-26 completions. He's grown into the perfect weapon for head coach Kyle Shanahan's unorthodox offense, and Sunday was the perfect showcase.

    "Brock, he didn't get rattled, which he really never does," Shanahan said after the game. "It's not like it's something new today to me with Brock. Brock's been like this since Day 1, and he's played at a very high level for a number of years now.".

    Recent findings suggest that purdy and Shanahan wisely used the Vikings' vicious aggressiveness against them. The NFL Next Gen Stats chart of Purdy's completions tells the tale; virtually all of his completions were within 10 yards of the line of scrimmage, meaning he got rid of the ball so quickly that Minnesota couldn't catch up. You can't record a sack when the ball's already downfield.

    "He just has this aura in the huddle," said Kittle, who caught Purdy's first two touchdown passes. "Everybody locks eyes with him, and we know every play, we have the chance to do something special.".

    "He's the best player in the game right now. He's super dialed in, the way he prepares, the way he competes," stated Evans, who caught Purdy's third touchdown pass of the night, late in the first half. "He's tough. I always thought he's been underrated — his precision. Super-smart player.".

    This 49ers team is something special, and not just because it has managed to win in three countries and two hemispheres this season. The Niners are in the meat of their schedule now; the Seahawks, Rams and Chiefs all await over the next five weeks. So too do teams like the Chargers, Eagles and Cardinals; San Francisco's schedule ranks 23rd in the NFL in terms of remaining difficulty, per Tankathon.

    Sources indicate that "We're halfway through this year. We've done some good things, but I mean, [the Super Bowl is] still to be determined," Shanahan remarked. "We know how we've been so far, but we're halfway there and we've got a long way to go.".

    Shanahan has led his teams to within sight of the promised land, reaching the Super Bowl as a head coach or coordinator on three separate occasions. In all three, the Lombardi Trophy eluded him. There's no reason to expect that this season will be any different … except for the fact that there was no reason to expect San Francisco would throw around the best defense in the league, either. The Irresistible Force rolls on.

    What's next for Red Sox after Jake Bauers deal? Plus more intel from the MLB GM Meetings

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (867 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings.
    • 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place?
    • For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings. The looming lockout, of course, played a major role in all of this.

    With Dec. 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place? What will it look like once it returns? How do you build a roster with such indeterminacy?

    For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.

    Industry observers note that tuesday (Nov. 17) is a significant date, marking the deadline for teams to decide which players to protect from the Rule 5 draft by adding them to their 40-man roster. Campbell, who did not appear in a significant-league game in 2026, is currently on the 40-man, signing an eight-year $60 million extension just eight games into his 2025 rookie campaign. But after his demotion in late June of that season, Campbell never found his way back to the majors.

    Now, with the lockout upon baseball, according to one source familiar with the situation, Campbell's 40-man spot might be in jeopardy.

    Boston is weighing the possibility of designating Campbell for assignment. When Craig Breslow, the Sox's president of baseball operations, was asked about that Tuesday, he brushed aside the question.

    "I'm not going to speak to that right now," he stated "Kristian's part of our organization. We're really happy about that, and we are invested in doing everything we can to get him to perform like he's capable of.".

    Now, if the Red Sox do DFA Campbell, the belief is that he would clear waivers, given his contract and lackluster performance at the minor-league level. Campbell is owed $55 million over the next six seasons, earning $13 million and $16 million over the 2031 and 2032 seasons, respectively. Campbell posted a .256/.383/.380 slash line with eight homers in 462 plate appearances at Triple-A in 2026.

    Because of those figures, one league executive suggested during the GM Meetings that their club would have no interest in Campbell. The exec took it a step further, confidently suggesting that they couldn't envision any team claiming the outfielder, considering the contract.

    Industry observers note that hypothetically, if Campbell is DFA'd, the Red Sox would free up a 40-man roster spot. If he clears waivers, Campbell, who has less than a year of MLB service time, would be outrighted to Triple-A Worcester. The Red Sox could then eventually add him back to the 40-man roster once they feel his production is worthy of another promotion to the parent club.

    None of this would provide the Red Sox with any financial relief unless another team were to claim him. Campbell's contract would still count toward their competitive balance tax payroll even if he were removed from the 40-man roster and remained in the minors.

    The risk-reward of such a move is something the Red Sox will also have to consider. Campbell has already acknowledged losing confidence following his recent struggles at both the major- and minor-league levels.

    Industry observers note that "He's got a world of potential," said Breslow. "We saw it in the minor leagues when he was coming up. We saw it in the first part of the season in [2025]. Then I think we started to see it in the second half last year, too, [at Worcester]. I still feel like he has a really bright substantial-league career ahead of him, and excited to get into spring training and see that manifest on the field.".

    The Red Sox signed Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million deal Friday, giving the club another power bat in their lineup. Willson Contreras will continue to anchor first base while Bauers will serve as the primary DH, filling in for Contreras from time to time.

    It has been revealed that bauers had a breakout season with the Brewers this year, batting .266/.389/.484 with an .874 OPS and 26 homers. The combo of plate discipline and damage in the strike zone intrigued the Red Sox. Furthermore, his ability to lift the ball in the air and use the entire field despite being a lefty gives the Red Sox confidence that he will be productive at Fenway.

    With Bauers part of the fold, though, Jarren Duran's future with the club is even more murky. The Sox are a heavily left-handed offensive club with Bauers, Wilyer Abreu, Masataka Yoshida, Roman Anthony, and Duran in the mix.

    One is likely going to have to go. And Duran, who could earn upwards of $11 million in arbitration next season, appears to be the most likely to be dealt.

    Even before the Bauers signing, multiple sources suggested during the GM Meetings that both the Red Sox and Duran might be better off parting ways via trade.

    Naturally, there is some apprehension.

    "I've been hearing for three years now about the outfield logjam that we have, but the reality is we haven't had all of our outfielders, including Masataka, healthy at the same time," Breslow stated. "These things have largely taken care of themselves, unfortunately.".

    As Liam Coen explains Jaguars' late field-goal decision, Giants take offense: 'Disrespectful as hell'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1671 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J.
    • Should he bank on his offense, which converted just once on six red-zone trips Sunday, to reverse course amid unfavorable down-and-distance?
    • Industry observers note that "Fourth-and-8 … what are those percentages of success?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Down eight points with 3:43 to play, the Jacksonville Jaguars faced fourth-and-goal from the 8-yard line.

    Head coach Liam Coen checked his charts.

    Should he bank on his offense, which converted just once on six red-zone trips Sunday, to reverse course amid unfavorable down-and-distance? Or should the Jaguars kick the 26-yard field goal, narrow their deficit to five points and trust the defense that held the Newly introduced York Giants to three points in the second half to get a stop?

    Industry observers note that "Fourth-and-8 … what are those percentages of success? I think they're probably less than 5 [percent] in a lot of ways in this league … " Coen said after the game. "Just executing that down-and-distance on a fourth down is kind of challenging, especially when they are zero-blitzing every play. The ball's going to come out. It's like a 'hope' play.".

    According to recent reports, so the Jaguars kicked the field goal and the Giants ran out the clock with two first downs. The Giants won 23-18 after leading for the final 47 minutes.

    "It just didn't work out," Coen said.

    Recent findings suggest that the Jaguars' strategy of relying on their defense during a day their offense struggled to maintain rhythm did not work out for the visiting team. But the strategy worked well to motivate a Giants team that had lost its own rhythm after halftime.

    If the Jaguars thought the Giants weren't going to realize the message their field goal sent, they were mistaken. New York quarterback J.J. McCarthy said "as an offense, we took that personal" as Jacksonville hedged on yet another New York implosion.

    Sources indicate that "100%, it's disrespectful as hell," right tackle Jermaine Eleumenor remarked from the postgame locker room. "You're kicking a field goal, you think you're going to get a stop on defense, and if I'm being honest, we were whooping them. On the line of scrimmage, they weren't winning. We won the line of scrimmage, both sides of the ball.".

    On a day in which the Jaguars were down starting center Robert Hainsey (knee) and lost starting left tackle Walker Little (knee) early in the fourth quarter, a pressure-happy Giants defense kept Trevor Lawrence from ever finding a rhythm.

    Arvell Reese brings the heat on Trevor Lawrence in the Giants' victory Sunday.

    And on a day in which the Jaguars were onboarding their trade-deadline acquisition starting defenders in defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III, the Giants capitalized on a group adjusting to complex schemes, including with quarterback keepers that powered each of their touchdown drives.

    So consider the Giants aware that they were 6-point betting underdogs at home and aware that plenty questioned their division-leading record on account of the below-.500 teams they had beaten.

    Giants head coach John Harbaugh called his team's sixth victory "the first real football win.".

    Edge rusher Abdul Carter remarked "everybody pretty much counted us out.".

    Sources indicate that "But we took that as disrespect, and we came out with a chip on our shoulder … " stated Carter, who finished the game with 2 sacks, 5 quarterback hits and 8 pressures, per Pro Football Focus. "I think we proved that we are worthy. They keep saying we can't beat these teams, we can't beat them. I don't know why they're saying that.

    "But what are they going to say now?".

    At the end of the first quarter, the Jaguars had not scored a touchdown.

    At the end of the second and then third, they hadn't either.

    This was a Jacksonville team that entered the week averaging 29.9 points per game, fourth in the league. Its 358.9 yards per game ranked ninth in total offense. So what explained the 20-6 deficit that trickled into the fourth quarter?

    Recent findings suggest that "I played really, really poorly today, and you're not going to win many games if I don't play better than that … " said Lawrence, who more than doubled his first three quarters' output with a 164-yard fourth quarter that brought his day to 301 yards, 1 touchdown and 2 interceptions on 25-of-47 (53.2%) passing. "As an offense as a whole, I thought we didn't come out with the aggressiveness and attacking that we normally have.

    "I felt like they punched us in the mouth a little bit.".

    Coen blamed himself for some of his early play-calling, saying he overcompensated for run calls he regretted a week prior by calling three straight passes to set up the opening drive's field goal. The Jaguars strayed on multiple drives from their run, which typically sets up their play-action passing and sets the tone for their physical offensive style. On third-and-medium-to-longs, the Giants pressured Lawrence to the tune of turnovers, incompletions and sacks.

    Facing third-and-6 with 7:45 to play in the first quarter, Lawrence thought he could hit receiver Parker Washington out of reach of cornerback Deonte Banks before realizing it was "just a really bad read, really bad decision.".

    With 11:08 to play in the fourth quarter, Lawrence aimed to throw high and early to avoid an approaching defensive lineman, instead throwing to a spot receiver Jakobi Meyers had yet to reach.

    The Giants turned the interceptions into six total points on a day they won by five.

    Yet when Jacksonville safety Antonio Johnson stripped running back Cam Skattebo and returned the fumble 42 yards, the Jaguars' offense responded with a turnover on downs. Complementary football eluded the team.

    By the time Lawrence found a rhythm in the fourth quarter, hitting receiver Brian Thomas Jr. for an 18-yard touchdown on third-and-10 sandwiched between two field-goal drives, the Jaguars' defense was waning. Perhaps matters would have been different if the officials had ruled differently on Washington's fourth-quarter catch in which he got two feet down but didn't secure the ball without movement as he fell to the ground; but even Lawrence admitted: "It was close, and you can't leave it in the ref's hands.".

    Industry observers note that the Giants celebrated holding onto a lead after letting their last contest slip away to the Washington Commanders in the final minute. Lawrence lamented that his offense's rally was too little, too late.

    "It was nice to see the fight at the end of the game and that we were still able to have a shot, thanks to our defense," Lawrence remarked. "We let our defense down today. They got us a bunch of turnovers and gave us plenty of opportunities to win the game, and we didn't capitalize.".

    At 6-3-1, the Giants maintained their grip on the NFC East even as the Cowboys improved to 5-6 with a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans. Next Gen Stats projects the Giants' chances of making the playoffs at 70% after the win.

    The Jaguars, meanwhile, don't just remain atop the AFC South at 7-3. Thanks to their three-game lead in the division, they carry a 98% chance of making the playoffs, per Next Gen Stats.

    Sources indicate that so postseason contention is not a front-of-mind problem. Cleaning up the errors that the Giants exposed, however, is.

    Less than two weeks after trading for Davis and Bates as indications of the belief in the 2026 Jaguars, Jacksonville coaches and executives continue to echo that message.

    It has been revealed that "They believe in this year and they believe that we can make a push to go to the Super Bowl," cornerback Jourdan Lewis told Yahoo Sports. "Those dreams are still intact, just getting accustomed to the guys and how we want to play and how to attack offenses and how they want to attack our system too. ….

    Instead, the Jaguars will continue working to acclimate Bates to split-safety looks that differ from his Atlanta responsibilities prior to the trade, and they'll work with Davis as he learns the nuances of coordinator Anthony Campanile's movement calls while remembering that gap integrity, physicality and winning in the trenches will always be the foundation for defensive-line success.

    The Jaguars were quiet as they shuffled into the postgame locker room from a rainy MetLife Field. But as they showered and packed up for their flight home, their tone reflected focus more than despair.

    There are holes to patch. There is time, in the seven remaining regular-season contests, to patch them.

    According to recent reports, "It's not the end of the world," Davis told Yahoo Sports of Coen's message. "We have to fix the complications. We have to take our medicine. We have to look ourselves in the mirror and then move forward the next week.

    Industry observers note that "You don't have time to dwell on your wins and losses in the previous week. You have to move on.".

    It has been revealed that so on the Jaguars will move from their five-point loss and on they'll move from Coen's decision to kick a field goal with 3:43 remaining. That decision will motivate Jacksonville's offensive players to show their head coach next time that they're capable of beating blitzes and performing even when the down and distance doesn't favor them.

    And the decision's failure will motivate Jacksonville's defense to shore up the assignments that ceded McCarthy a 19-yard completion up the middle and Skattebo a 5-yard run on second-and-5 to seal the win.

    Several Jaguars players echoed their trust in Coen on that decision and beyond. And Lawrence, who said he struggled to read the field efficiently until late in the game, said he understood which part of those late-game analytics moments were in his control.

    "It's not my decision at the end of the day," Lawrence stated. "It's coach's, but I stand by him. We've got to make plays on first, second and third down so we have a chance to go for it not on fourth-and-7 or 8. It's just a tough down ….

    "We know who we are. We just didn't play well tonight. If you don't play well, you get beat.".

    #73306. 10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1650 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1650 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 20, is an key date on MLB's offseason calendar.
    • Sources indicate that dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary.
    • Industry observers note that with that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This Friday, Nov. 20, is an key date on MLB's offseason calendar. It is the deadline for teams to offer 2027 contracts to their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players. The player does not have to sign by Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline, but he must be offered a contract. If he's not, the player is considered non-tendered and immediately becomes a free agent.

    Sources indicate that dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary. Adolis García, Nathaniel Lowe, Alek Manoah, and Christopher Morel were among the notable non-tenders last offseason. Go back a few years and big names like Cody Bellinger and Kyle Schwarber were non-tendered.

    Industry observers note that with that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors. You can be sure these teams will scour the trade market for these players and try to get something back before making the non-tender official.

    Projected salary: $11.1 million (team control through 2028).

    Industry observers note that duran was a non-tender candidate even before the Jake Bauers signing pushed him out of the everyday lineup. There is no such thing as too many good players, but the Red Sox now have two first basemen (Bauers and Willson Contreras) and four outfielders (Duran, Wilyer Abreu, Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela). Mickey Gasper and Masataka Yoshida are still around too. That's eight players for five lineup spots (first base, DH, three outfield spots). On any given day, three of those guys will be on the bench. Duran, who got MVP votes in 2024, had a 20-20 season in 2026, but it came with a ballooning strikeout rate and a .266 on-base percentage. He has been on the trade block for close to two years now and the writing is on the wall. If the Red Sox are unable to trade Duran this week, there's a real chance he'll get non-tendered Friday given his hefty salary projection.

    Projected salary: $7.7 million (team control through 2028).

    Former No. 1 overall draft picks have been non-tendered in the past (Tim Beckham most recently), just not by the team that drafted them. Non-tendering Torkelson would be a tough look for the Tigers even though he has not developed into the impact hitter he was projected to be coming out of Arizona State. Simply put, the salary is beginning to outweigh the production. Torkelson, 27, is a 25-30 homer bat with one of the league's highest strikeout rates, middling on-base percentages, and no secondary value (defense, baserunning, etc.). That stated, the Tigers do not have an obvious replacement first baseman ready to step in (Colt Keith was the backup in 2026). That, plus the fact that Torkelson has No. 1 pick pedigree, could keep him in Detroit another year.

    Projected salary: $2.3 million (team control through 2029).

    It has been revealed that the American League Rookie of the Year in 2024, Gil has battled injuries and ineffectiveness in the two seasons since. The swing-and-miss rate on his fastball went from an elite 28.5% in 2024 to a below-average 18.8% in 2025 and 17.4% in 2026. Gil, 28, spent time in Triple-A this past season and the Yankees moved him into the bullpen late in the year, where the results were so-so. The salary projection is a pittance, particularly for a team with New York's payroll, though Gil is now out of minor-league options (he must pass through waivers to go to Triple-A) and doesn't have an obvious role. Because he is a pitcher and breathing, and also has a major award win in the not-too-distant past, the Yankees might be able to find a trade partner this week. If not, Gil is a definite non-tender candidate.

    Projected salary: $7.6 million (team control through 2028).

    A fan favorite and an All-Star this past season, Clement crashed hard in the second half, and the fact of the matter is he has a .295 on-base percentage in his three full seasons with the Blue Jays. Also, the soon-to-be 31-year-old's defensive numbers tumbled this year. Clement's contact skills are elite and he's a versatile, high-energy player. As a utility guy, he's an ace. As an everyday player, he's stretched. Clement's projected salary is hefty for a utility player, particularly one with limited offensive upside who no longer reliably catches the baseball. My guess is the Blue Jays will keep him and live with the salary, but it's not an obvious decision.

    Projected salary: $5.1 million (team control through 2028).

    Similar to Torkelson, non-tendering a former No. 1 overall pick would be a tough look for the Twins, but a clean break might be best for all involved at this point. Lewis, 27, has trended down since his boffo second half in 2023, enough that he was sent to Triple-A for a spell this summer. He's also moved down the defensive spectrum from third base to first base. It's not due to a lack of effort; Lewis is a major tinkerer who has tried all sorts of swing adjustments. It just hasn't come together. A fresh start elsewhere, away from the spotlight of former No. 1 pick and face of the franchise, might be best for him. The budget-conscious Twins could then reallocate the projected $5.1 million elsewhere on the roster. Right now, they can't count on Lewis to hit or have a meaningful impact defensively.

    Projected salary: $3.4 million (team control through 2028).

    It has been revealed that in 2023, Gorman slugged 27 home runs and looked like one of baseball's top young power hitters. In the three seasons since, he has not come close to repeating that success. The hope was that moving him to third base, his natural position, would unlock Gorman's offense following the Nolan Arenado trade. That didn't happen, and Gorman spent a substantial chunk of the summer in Triple-A, where he continued to have a hard time making contact. Now 26, Gorman has a minor-league option remaining and can go to Triple-A again in 2027, but the signs are not subtle. The Cardinals are reportedly seeking a stopgap third baseman until top prospect Jesús Báez is ready, which would likely not be the case if they had any belief in Gorman. That projected $3.4 million salary is a high price for a reclamation project ticketed for the minors.

    Projected salary: $6.9 million (team control through 2028).

    According to recent reports, right-handed power is in short supply throughout baseball and Burger, 31 in April, has hit at least 28 home runs in three of the last four years. He is a one-tool player, though. The home runs come with low batting averages, low on-base percentages, higher-than-average strikeout rates, and little to no defensive or baserunning value. Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young said his team lacked "grit and toughness," whatever that means, and indicated he wants more hitters who grind out at-bats. That's not Burger, who can hit the ball a mile but is not known for making life tough on pitchers. The $6.9 million projection could be deemed too pricey for a player with such a limited skill set.

    Projected salary: $6.6 million (team control through 2027).

    Doval went from the Yankees to the Pirates at the trade deadline, then from the Pirates to the Giants on waivers in September. He's a former All-Star who led the National League in saves in 2023, two things that have boosted his arbitration salaries. Since 2023, Doval has been a middle reliever who was on the outside of the Circle of Trust™ more often than not. The 29-year-old righty still throws very hard. There's nothing wrong with his arm. It's hard to believe he gets hit as hard as he does sometimes. Doval earned $6.1 million in 2026 and a player cannot have a salary cut by more than 20% during his team control years. That would set Doval's minimum 2027 salary at $4.88 million. I wonder if the Giants would offer him a pay cut, say $5.5M or so, and tell him it's either that or a non-tender. That happens a few times a year around the league.

    Projected salary: $6.5 million (team control through 2027).

    In a recent development, A fan favorite in San Diego -- "Ho-ly Sheets!" chants are commonplace during his at-bats at Petco Park -- Sheets has fallen by the wayside a bit with the Padres, so much so that he started just one of their six postseason games this year. The 30-year-old is a platoon player who is good against righties more than great and is a defensive liability at both first base and left field. Realistically, Sheets is a platoon DH, and teams rarely pay well for that role unless they're confident they will get substantial offensive numbers. In the grand scheme of things, the projected $6.5 million isn't much. It is top-of-the-market dollars for this skill set, however.

    Projected salary: $1.4 million (team control through 2029).

    Recent findings suggest that two years ago, Blanco threw a no-hitter in his eighth career start. This year, he was so far out of the picture that he pitched once in Houston's last 12 games (two innings at the end of a 13-2 blowout), and the Astros opted to start Peter Lambert on two days' rest with a postseason spot on the line in Game 162. Blanco, who is older than you may realize (he turned 33 in August), returned from Tommy John surgery this summer and had a rough go of it. The pitching-needy Astros could send him to Triple-A next season, as he has a minor-league option remaining, but his stuff was diminished after surgery, and again, they didn't trust him late in the year. You would be surprised at how many cheap pitchers get non-tendered every year. Blanco could join them this week.

    Jayson Tatum misses game-winner in loss to Warriors as Celtics continue on worst losing skid since 2021

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (517 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Boston Celtics, thanks to a substantial defensive stand from Draymond Green late, are now on their worst losing skid in years.
    • It has been revealed that the Celtics fell to the Golden State Warriors 88-87 on Sunday night at the Chase Center in San Francisco.
    • It had gone a ridiculous 429 games without a four-game losing skid, which was the second-longest stretch in franchise history.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Boston Celtics, thanks to a substantial defensive stand from Draymond Green late, are now on their worst losing skid in years.

    It has been revealed that the Celtics fell to the Golden State Warriors 88-87 on Sunday night at the Chase Center in San Francisco. That was Boston's fourth straight loss, which marked the first time the franchise had lost four consecutive games since May 2021.

    It had gone a ridiculous 429 games without a four-game losing skid, which was the second-longest stretch in franchise history. The Celtics once went 468 games from 1962-68.

    According to recent reports, boston led by as many as 11 late in the third quarter, and seemed in a great spot to grab the win. But the Warriors chipped away and got back into the game, and even took the lead on a Brandin Podziemski 3-pointer with about 2:30 left in the contest. Those were the last points the Warriors scored.

    With just eight seconds left, Tatum had a great look to win the game. Down by a point, Tatum drove at Green and took a fadeaway jumper from the elbow. The shot was off the mark, and he finished going 0 of 7 from the field in the second half.

    Industry observers note that podziemski led the Warriors with 18 points and seven rebounds in the win, which moved them to 9-8 on the season and ended a five-game losing streak of their own. Charles Bassey added 13 points and nine rebounds, and Green finished with nine points. The Warriors are still missing Stephen Curry, who is sidelined with an abdominal injury.

    Industry observers note that tatum finished with 27 points and 10 rebounds while shooting 8 of 20 from the field. Derrick White had 14 points, and Luka Garza added 10 off the bench. They were the only three Celtics to hit double figures, and the 87 points they managed as a team were the fewest they've scored all season.

    The Celtics had double-digit leads in three of their four losses, including a 17-point lead over the Denver Nuggets before blowing that contest Wednesday. They were up by 13 points at Sacramento on Saturday before Keegan Murray sank a put-back jumper to seal the one-point win.

    Boston got the losing streak started Monday in a 10-point loss to the Orlando Magic, who rallied late to grab the win at TD Garden.

    While the losing streak isn't great, it's far from the time to be concerned for the Celtics. It's not even December yet, and they sit at 11-6 on the season. That's good for third in the Eastern Conference standings, behind only the Philadelphia 76ers and Atlanta Hawks. There is plenty of time for the Celtics to rebound from this stretch and maintain their position in the East. And, the longest losing streak in NBA history is 28 games. The Celtics aren't even close to that mark.

    But their run of keeping losing streaks to a minimum has ended. They'll have a chance to snap the four-game losing skid Tuesday night against the Washington Wizards.

    2027 Baseball Hall of Fame ballot released: 8 things to know, including newcomers, trends and a prediction

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1171 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.
    • The full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman.
    • As a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.

    The full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman. Newcomers to the ballot are in bold.

    As a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class. Those who get at least 5% of the vote can remain on the ballot the following year, and so on, for a maximum of 10 voting cycles. Players who are on the ballot for 10 years without getting 75% of the vote, in addition to players not getting 5% of the vote, fall off the ballot in ensuing years, though that doesn't mean the doors to the Hall are permanently shut.

    The results will be announced on Jan. 19, with the induction set for Cooperstown over the summer.

    Here's everything else you need to know about the Baseball Hall of Fame this offseason.

    Sources indicate that as alluded to earlier, there are two different votes each offseason. The BBWAA vote is for former players who have been retired from Major League Baseball for at least five years. It's the most common method in mainstream Hall of Fame ballot discussions. When you hear stuff like "first-ballot Hall of Famer," it means via the BBWAA vote.

    According to recent reports, players who don't make it via the BBWAA vote can get extra chances via committees. That's how, for example, Jeff Kent made it last year. Formerly called the Veterans Committee, the Hall of Fame now uses Era Committees, which are divided into two categories: contemporary baseball (1980 to present) and classic (prior to 1980). The contemporary ballot is then split into two, one for players and one for non-players like umpires, executives, pioneers and managers.

    Sure enough, this time around, it is a non-player Contemporary Baseball Committee, which looks at "managers, umpires and executives whose most significant career impact was realized since 1980.".

    We'll dive further into this group as we get closer to the Dec. 6 vote.

    In a recent development, giants legend Buster Posey joins the ballot, and he's one of those cases where I don't think a bunch of people need to delve deeply into his numbers. More than statistics, sometimes we get "feel" guys, as in, you just know he's a Hall of Famer. Posey qualifies there, I would think, for 75% of the electorate. We'll obviously do a deeper dive in the coming weeks, but even without the longevity component (Posey only played in parts of 12 MLB seasons), I think he's in.

    As for the rest of the first-timers, the best case would be Jon Lester. Given the way a lot of similar starting pitchers have been treated in voting in recent years, my hunch is he'll be able to hang around on the ballot, but he has a major uphill battle in order to get in.

    Then you're looking at Brett Gardner, Ryan Zimmerman, Kyle Seager, the short peak of Jake Arrieta and relief work of Andrew Miller. Good players worth mentioning, of course, but they won't sniff the Hall and it seems likely all behind Posey and Lester are one-and-dones on this ballot, as they'll fall short of 5% of the vote.

    This is the sixth year for Alex Rodriguez on the ballot, which means it's the sixth time that I point out that we don't really need much time to go over his case. His numbers say he's one of the 10 best position players of all time, but his ties to PEDs are keeping him out to this point.

    It has been revealed that he did rise from 37.1% of the vote in 2025 to 40% last time, a new high-water mark. The progress is too modest to believe it's trending toward him getting in, but the number this year is certainly worth watching. If he somehow makes a leap to the 50% range, a deeper conversation might be in order.

    In a recent development, while some voters don't mind sending in blank ballots to prove some sort of nebulous point, most impose limits on themselves. Whether it's the actual rule of 10 or some voters saying they'll only vote, for example, for a maximum of three players on any given ballot, relatively weak ballots can leave openings for the best players to show huge gains. With Carlos Beltràn and Andruw Jones getting in last year and only one strong first-year candidate, perhaps Chase Utley can benefit.

    Utley is only in his fourth year on the ballot, but he's already made significant gains:.

    Recent findings suggest that he only needs to add 15.9 points after jumping nearly 20 last voting cycle. The situation is ripe for Utley to either get all the way in or get close enough to where he probably makes the Hall of Fame in 2028.

    Some of us are pushing to lower the Hall of Fame standard on modern starting pitchers, given the decreases in workload and how it affects their career numbers. We might be making some headway, but it's still tough sledding. Here are the holdover starting pitchers and their standing:.

    The bar for relievers to make the Hall of Fame is justly pretty high. We recently saw Billy Wagner make a late move and make it in his last try on the BBWAA ballot. Francisco Rodríguez has had four chances on the ballot and gotten between 7.8% and 11.8% of the vote thus far.

    In a recent development, K-Rod ranks sixth all time in saves and has good rate stats. He's worth tracking as it relates to three active relievers. Kenley Jansen is third in saves with a similar number of innings pitched to K-Rod. Craig Kimbrel is fifth and has more than 100 fewer innings pitched. Aroldis Chapman is ninth and in the ballpark of Kimbrel in workload to this point.

    If K-Rod continues to have trouble making headway toward induction, does that mean Kimbrel and Chapman will have trouble as well? What about Jansen?

    According to recent reports, who else is back on the ballot? A quick look:.

    In a recent development, posey is a lock. If the committee era chooses Bochy, Baker and/or Sabean, that would be some nice San Francisco flavor, too, right? I'll predict that committee ballot at a later date, though.

    I'll also say Utley's good roll here continues with a relatively weak ballot (at least when you factor in what the PED stain has done to some guys).

    On the player side, my 2027 Hall of Fame class prediction is Buster Posey and Chase Utley.

    Latest Update: Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

    📅 31 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1116 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • Industry observers note that kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • In a recent development, just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    Industry observers note that kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    In a recent development, just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    In a recent development, kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    Recent findings suggest that it's vital to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    It has been revealed that right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    In a recent development, we already know the Wild are substantial-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    Recent findings suggest that with Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't at the moment have on their roster.

    Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    According to recent reports, utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    According to recent reports, allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

    • Hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving. In Major League Baseball, that usually means a slow news week. Those of us wanting a flurry of moves before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 are starting to lose a little hope, but hey, it's still possible. We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition.

    In a recent development, as for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov. 16, let's go.

    Sources indicate that the Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner. They have extended a qualifying offer to Trevor Rogers and though he's expected to decline it, a reunion remains possible. If not, the Orioles are also reportedly interested in lefty free agents Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd and David Peterson.

    Recent findings suggest that rogers is the best option here. He finished last season with a 2.90 ERA in his last 20 starts. CBS Sports ranked him as the No. 3 free agent this offseason and the best non-Tarik Skubal pitcher on the market. Here's part of the write-up:.

    Sources indicate that rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years.

    Recent findings suggest that as things stand, the Orioles' rotation starts with right-handers Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Cade Povich is a left-handed option, but they'd clearly like someone else who could qualify as a frontline starter from the left-handed side.

    Former Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara has been involved in trade rumors for years and the Marlins never end up moving him. More of the same this offseason? Probably.

    "I expect Sandy to be on the Marlins next year," general manager Peter Bendix told MLB Network.

    Industry observers note that alcantara, 31, was 13-11 with a 3.87 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 153 strikeouts in an MLB-best 214 innings last season. He also grabbed three saves down the stretch as the Marlins started experimenting with using starters in relief on their bullpen day between starts. The 2022 Cy Young winner missed all of 2024 after having Tommy John surgery and started to show flashes of his old self last season. He's now making $21 million in 2027 before hitting free agency.

    If the Marlins contend, he'll surely stay put, but if they fall out of contention, it'll be another round of trade rumors.

    Free agent left-hander A.J. Minter is getting a lot of interest, per MLB Network. Coming off a season in which he was productive for both the Mets and Twins (in all, a 2.56 ERA, 1.05 WHIP and 41 strikeouts in 45 ⅔ innings), he's being chased by at least the Blue Jays, Nationals, Phillies, Rangers and Royals.

    According to recent reports, though he's closed on occasion, Minter has been a quality setup man for most of his 10 MLB years, especially with the Braves in the 2020-24 range. He has good playoff numbers, too, with a 2.88 ERA in 20 career postseason appearances.

    Sources indicate that the Brewers have acquired right-handed reliever Ryan Walker from the Giants for two minor-league pitchers, the team declared late Sunday. Walker, 30, was up and down in his four years with the Giants, which included time as a closer. He had a 1.91 ERA, 10 saves and 2.8 WAR in 2024, but lost the job of closer during a sub-par 2025 season. Last year, he pitched to a 7.16 ERA and 1.81 WHIP in 32 ⅔ innings.

    We have plenty of examples of the Brewers buying low on a player and ending up getting the best version of him, so Walker is the latest to keep an eye on here.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
    • How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
    • According to recent reports, so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the fresh signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

    How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

    According to recent reports, so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

    According to recent reports, title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

    First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    Industry observers note that another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

    “They are really good examples,” Arteta stated. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

    Industry observers note that “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

    In a recent development, you could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

    It has been revealed that it can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

    Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

    You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

    Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

    In a recent development, here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s upcoming £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

    When Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

    In a recent development, it should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

    Recent findings suggest that city, in contrast to their opponents, demonstrated a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where fresh boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

    Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

    Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

    Industry observers note that throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

    Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

    Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

    Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D.

    According to recent reports, had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal showed was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

    “I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

    You would be brave to say it will be their last.

    Referee Sam Barrott (Yorkshire).

    According to recent reports, it’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

    I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

    In a recent development, A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we highlighted, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

    He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

    Sources indicate that I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

    The feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning.     #73289. Which team needs Tarik Skubal the most? Ranking the suitors for the best free agent available

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1171 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Which team needs Tarik Skubal the most? Ranking the suitors for the best free agent available

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1171 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec.
    • Sources indicate that the decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No.
    • "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec. 1 lockout of the players by MLB owners, we might see an accelerated pace of activity soon. The most tantalizing possibility is that ace and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the undisputed top talent on the free agent market this winter, will sign before the sport shuts down for an indeterminate amount of time.

    Sources indicate that the decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No. 1 free agent of the 2026-27 class, and it's not an especially close call. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He showed few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    Will he set the record for the biggest contract ever signed by a pitcher? Will Skubal fetch the highest average annual salary for a pitcher? Will he top $400 million? Those are all reasonable questions to ask. First, though, there's a question to be asked about the teams that are already pursuing him the most vigorously. That question is, which team needs him the most? We're restricting our discussion to the five teams that have been most reliably linked to Skubal so far this offseason. We're already hearing reports of surprise teams, and it's always possible a surprise late bidder will enter the fray and even win his signature, but for now, these five clubs are the favorites. This, then, is an ordering of those teams based on which desperately needs a talent like Skubal in order to reach their goals in 2027 and beyond. Let's get to it, in order from "needs him the most" to "needs him but not as urgently as the teams ahead of them" ….

    Recent findings suggest that the Cubs are in contention mode and in need of roster improvements if they're going to run down the world champion Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central. The rotation is without question the most pressing need for Chicago. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, David Peterson, and deadline acquisition Clay Holmes are all free agents. Justin Steele hasn't taken the mound at the big-league level since early in the 2025 season thanks to UCL surgery and a halting recovery process. While he's expected to be ready for 2027, he's not exactly a known quantity right now. Young upsider Cade Horton may not be back until midseason after undergoing Tommy John surgery, and Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery, may be on a similar timeline. So, yes, the Cubs need a lot of rotation help, and Skubal would give them the true frontline ace they'd lack even if everyone were healthy. Unfortunately for the Cubs fans, it sounds like the Ricketts aren't willing to be truly competitive for his services.

    Coming off the grave disappointments of 2026, the Mets could certainly use a headline-grabbing addition to improve their chances in 2027 and inspire a surely disaffected fan base. Beyond that, the Mets need more starting pitching to accompany promising young Nolan McLean. Christian Scott seems like a lock, but he doesn't project as a frontliner. They have some depth options for the back end, but they need a true needle-mover like Skubal at the very front. That's especially the case in what figures to be a hotly competitive NL East in 2027. Thus far, David Stearns and owner Steve Cohen sound committed to making a good-faith run at Skubal.

    The Padres have a lot of work to do if they're going to earn a fourth straight playoff appearance. Speaking of which, the rotation is crying out for help right about now. They lost Dylan Cease to free agency last winter, and this time Michael King may be bound elsewhere, too. The Pads declined their club option on Nick Pivetta, and while they hope to bring him back on more favorable terms, there's no guarantee they'll be able to do that. Yes, Joe Musgrove will be back, but how much can he give them and how effective will he be? They'll need even more help if Adrian Morejon, a lockdown bulk reliever and possible starter-conversion project, signs elsewhere. Skubal's made to order, and signing the top talent on the market would be a strong signal by new owners José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones that the team's recent tradition of spending and contending won't be fading away.

    Industry observers note that the Dodgers self-evidently needed Skubal enough to acquire him from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the deadline and do so at significant cost. On paper, the Dodgers aren't as desperate for rotation help as the teams ahead of them on this list, but there's still a need. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is a certifiable ace, but behind him Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are established health and durability risks. Shohei Ohtani is something of an unknown, at least insofar as his pitching is concerned right now, and thus far Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan have not proved worthy of being relied upon. One can squint and see the Dodgers' current championship window closing in the reasonably near future, which means that's all the more reason to push the chips in now. Retaining the elite services of Skubal would greatly aid the cause in 2027.

    Sources indicate that eyeball a rotation that already includes Dylan Cease, José Soriano, and Trey Yesavage, and you might think it doesn't need much more. And maybe it doesn't. As a matter of principle, though, any team with contending aspirations should be interested in a top-shelf ace when he hits the market.
